properties.description:
FOLDED INTO `req:a-report-says-what-it-swept-and-whether-its-checks-ran` on Anthony's word, because it is the same theme arriving from a different direction: `propose_heal` could not say whether its scorer RAN, and the toolsnap gate could not say WHAT IT READ.

THE DEFECT (`fact:defect-the-toolsnap-gate-defaults-to-a-binary-nobody-rebuilt`): `tools/toolsnap.py` defaulted `--bin` to `target/debug/reflow2-mcp` and printed 'ALL 149 TOOLSNAPS MATCH' against whatever build happened to be there. Found by accident — a tool description was changed, RELEASE was rebuilt, and the gate reported the surface unchanged while the committed snapshot still held the old text.

THE FIX IS OUTPUT, NOT POLICY: every verdict — match, drift AND regenerate — now ends with the binary it read and that binary's build time, and adds a loud STALE warning naming the offending file when any `crates/**/src/*.rs` is newer.

⚠️ THE DEFAULT DELIBERATELY STAYS `target/debug`, which is the opposite of the obvious fix and the reason is measured: `ci.yml:93` runs `cargo build -p reflow2-mcp` — a debug build — in the same job before the toolsnap step at `:142`. Pointing the default at release would aim CI at a binary it never builds, converting a local-only defect into a CI one. This also CORRECTS the first version of the fact, which left CI's exposure unestablished: CI was never exposed.

MTIME IS A WEAK SIGNAL AND IS USED ACCORDINGLY. Git operations can leave sources older than a build — which is exactly why the launch wrapper hashes CONTENT instead — so mtime here only ever ADDS a warning and never suppresses one. A false negative therefore costs nothing that was not already lost, and a false positive costs one rebuild.

DEMONSTRATED LIVE, BOTH DIRECTIONS, on the working tree that produced it: against the stale binary the gate printed the STALE warning naming `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/tools/query.rs`; after `cargo build -p reflow2-mcp` the same command printed the verdict and the binary line with no warning. So the case fires and the counterweight is silent, measured rather than asserted.

NOT DONE: `tools/toolsnap.py` is not a registered Artifact, so this change moved no checksum and the design records it against `cmp:packaging` instead. Several gate scripts are in that position and nobody has decided whether they should be registered.
properties.name: The toolsnap gate names the binary it compared against and warns when source is newer — folded into the same theme as propose_heal's vacuous zero
